rules.evidence: FAA's SDRS FAQ states that records must complete the Quality Control review process before becoming available in the public processed-report search. Submission therefore precedes or equals an unknown later public-availability point and is not itself publication evidence.
rules.rule: Never copy SubmissionDate into available_at. A dated artifact proving completed QC/public availability is required.

rules.evidence: DifficultyDate identifies when the service difficulty occurred; FAA public availability happens only after submission and completion of the Quality Control review process.

rules.field: ApprovalDate or other approval-like administrative timestamp
rules.evidence: The public research performed to date has not established an FAA field definition proving that an approval-like timestamp in any export is exactly the moment the record completed public-facing Quality Control and became searchable.
rules.rule: Do not infer public release semantics from a field name. Promote only if an FAA schema/manual or archived public artifact establishes the meaning for the relevant period.

rules.field: current annual CSV row and fields
rules.evidence: FAA currently publishes yearly SDR CSV downloads, but current presence does not establish when the row or its present field values first completed QC and became public.
rules.rule: Treat current CSV presence as current-source evidence only. Historical cutoff admission requires an archived release or record-specific publication evidence.

default_rule.rule: Without explicit public-release timing or an immutable archived public snapshot containing the record/field value, historical SDR availability remains unknown and is excluded from strict PIT backtests.
